Question: According to Genesis 3:2–3, which tree did God tell Adam and Eve not to eat from?
C: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil

Question: According to Genesis 3:1–5, what did the serpent cause Eve to question?
C: What God had commanded about the tree

A: She would leave the garden immediately
B: Her eyes would be opened and she would know good and evil
C: The earth would stop producing food

Question: According to Genesis 3:6, what attracted Eve to the forbidden fruit?
A: It had been offered by an angel
B: It grew on the tallest tree
C: It looked good for food, pleasant to the eyes, and desirable for wisdom
D: Adam had already eaten from it

Question: According to Genesis 3:6, after Eve ate the fruit, what did she do?
B: She hid it beneath the tree
C: She gave some to her husband, and he ate
D: She offered it to the animals

Question: According to Genesis 3:7, what did Adam and Eve realize after eating the fruit?
C: The serpent had left Eden

Question: According to Genesis 3:7, what did Adam and Eve use to make coverings?
C: Palm branches

Question: According to Genesis 3:8, how did Adam and Eve respond when they heard God in the garden?
C: They began building a house

Question: According to Genesis 3:9, what question did God ask Adam when calling to him?
C: Why did you plant a tree?

Question: According to Genesis 3:10, why did Adam say he was afraid?
C: Because the serpent was gone
D: Because he had lost his way

Question: According to Genesis 3:11, what did God ask Adam after Adam said he was naked?
A: Why did you leave the garden?
B: Who told you that you were naked?
C: Where is the serpent?
D: Why did you hide the fruit?

Question: According to Genesis 3:12, whom did Adam blame when God asked about the forbidden fruit?
C: The woman God gave to be with him

Question: According to Genesis 3:13, what explanation did Eve give for eating the fruit?
B: She did not know the tree existed
C: The fruit fell into her hands

Question: According to Genesis 3:14, what was one consequence God pronounced on the serpent?
A: It would leave the earth forever
B: It would be unable to speak to animals

B: Pain in bringing forth children would be multiplied
C: She would no longer hear God
D: She would have to build a city

Question: According to Genesis 3:17, what did God say was cursed because of Adam?
C: The river

Question: According to Genesis 3:18, what would the ground bring forth for Adam?
C: Only fruit trees

Question: According to Genesis 3:17–19, how would Adam’s work change because of his disobedience?

B: He would eat from the ground through painful toil

Question: According to Genesis 3:19, what did God tell Adam about his return to the ground?

Question: According to Genesis 3:15, what conflict did God say would exist between the serpent and the woman?
B: A dispute over the garden trees
C: A battle between Adam and the angels

Question: According to Genesis 3:20, why did Adam call his wife Eve?
A: Because she was the mother of all living
C: Because she made the first garden
D: Because she spoke to the serpent

Question: According to Genesis 3:21, what did the Lord God make for Adam and Eve?
C: A pair of sandals
D: Tunics of skin to clothe them

B: Till the ground from which he was taken
C: Care for the animals

B: To guard the way to the tree of life
